name: Papua New Guinea
summary: A diagonal division with a red upper-fly triangle bearing a yellow bird of paradise, and a black lower-hoist triangle with the Southern Cross in white stars. Designed by a 15-year-old schoolgirl, Susan Karike Huhume.
origin: In 1970 the territory's administration proposed a design, but local opposition led to a competition. Susan Karike Huhume, then a 15-year-old student, submitted the winning design, adopted on 1 July 1971, four years before independence from Australia in 1975.

symbols.name: Raggiana bird of paradise
symbols.description: A yellow bird in flight with long plumes.
symbols.meaning: The emergence of Papua New Guinea into nationhood.

symbols.name: Southern Cross
symbols.description: Five white stars in the black triangle.
symbols.meaning: The country's place in the South Pacific and its links with Australia and other southern nations.

facts: Its designer was 15 years old when she won the competition.
It is one of the few national flags with a bird of paradise.
Papua New Guinea has over 800 languages, more than any other country.
clues: A diagonal split of red with a yellow bird of paradise and black with the Southern Cross.
Adopted four years before independence from Australia.
